source_text: λῆς Ἰούδα, καὶ ἐνέπλησα αὐτὸν Πνεῦμα θεῖον σοφίας καὶ συνέσεως καὶ ἐπιστήμης. Καὶ ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ διανοεῖσθαι τὸ χρυσίον, καὶ τὸ ἀργύριον, καὶ τὸν χαλκὸν, καὶ τὴν ὑάκινθον, καὶ τὴν πορφύραν, καὶ τὸ κόκκινον τὸ νηστὸν, καὶ τὴν βύσσον τὴν κεκλωσμένην, καὶ τὰ λιθουργικὰ, καὶ εἰς τὰ ἔργα τὰ τεκτονικὰ τῶν ξύλων ἐργάζεσθαι κατὰ πάντα τὰ ἔργα. Καὶ ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτὸν, καὶ τὸν Ἐλιὰβ τοῦ Ἀχισαμὰ, ἐκ φυλῆς Δὰν, καὶ παντὶ συνετῷ καρδίᾳ δέδωκα σύνεσιν, καὶ ποιήσουσιν πάντα ὅσα συνέταξα.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅπως καθηγεῖται μὲν τῶν τεχνουργημάτων ὁ Βεσελεὴλ, Ἐλιὰβ δὲ ἐργάζεται. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί οὖν τοῦτό γε; {ΚΥΡ.} Πεύσῃ δὴ οὖν· Ἰούδας τε καὶ Δὰν, ἄμφω μὲν ἐξ Ἰακὼβ, ἀλλ' ὁ μὲν ἐξ ἐλευθέρας τῆς Λείας, ὁ δὲ ἐκ θεραπαίνης τῆς Βάλης. Τύπος οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἐναργὴς ὁ Βεσελεὴλ τοῦ πεφηνότος ἡμῖν ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα τὸ κατὰ σάρκα Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἐκ φύσεως ἀληθῶς τῆς ἐλευθέρας, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τῆς θείας καὶ ὑπερτάτης. Ἐμφήνειε δ' ἂν εὖ μάλα καὶ Ἐλιὰβ τοὺς, ὡς ἐκ δούλης τῆς Ἰερουσαλὴμ, Χριστῷ συνεργασαμένους ἀποστόλους καὶ εὐαγγελιστάς· Θεοῦ γὰρ γεγόνασι συνεργοὶ τὰ εἰς σύστασιν τῶν ἁγίων Ἐκκλησιῶν μονονουχὶ πονοῦντι καὶ τεχνωμένῳ Συνεκόμιζον δὲ τὰ ἐξ οἰκείας σπουδῆς καὶ ἐπιεικείας εἰς τὰ τῆς σκηνῆς ἔργα πάντες οἱ συνετοὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, τῶν κατὰ καιροὺς διδασκάλων ἀποπληροῦντες εἰκόνας, οἷς ἐν σπουδῇ καὶ φροντίδι τὸ ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ ὅσαπερ ἂν τελοίη πρὸς ὄνησιν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας Χριστοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: [Completes Exodus 31:2 from §31: phy|lēs Iouda.] '…[tri]be of Judah, and eneplēsa (I filled) him with Pneuma theion of sophia, synesis and epistēmē. And en panti ergō dianoeisthai (to devise in every work) the chrysion, argyrion, chalkos, the hyakinthos (blue/violet), the porphyra (purple), the kokkinon to nēston (spun scarlet), the byssos hē keklōsmenē (twisted fine linen), the lithourgika (stoneworks), and eis ta erga ta tektonika tōn xylōn (carpentry of woods) ergazesthai kata panta ta erga. And I dedōka (have given/appointed) him, and Eliab [son] of Achisama, ek phylēs Dan, and to every synetō kardia (understanding in heart) dedōka synesin, and they shall poiēsousin all hosa synetaxa (that I ordered).' Athrei (look) how kathēgeitai (leads) tōn technourgēmatōn (the craftworks) Bezalel, but Eliab ergazetai (works). PALL.: Ti oun touto ge (what then is this)? CYR.: Peusē (you will learn). Judah and Dan, both ex Iakōb, but the one ex eleutheras (of the free woman) Leah, the other ek therapainēs (of a maidservant) Bilhah (Balē). Typos enargēs (a clear type), then, is Bezalel of the one pephēnotos (having appeared) to us ek phylēs Iouda to kata sarka (as to the flesh), Christ, and ek physeōs alēthōs tēs eleutheras (from the truly free nature), dēlon hoti (clearly) the theia kai hypertatē (divine and most high). Eliab emphēneie an (would indicate) eu mala those who, hōs ek doulēs tēs Ierousalēm (as from the slave Jerusalem), Christō synergasamenous (worked with Christ), apostolous kai euangelistas; for they gegonasi synergoi of God, who mononouchi (all but) ponounti kai technōmenō (toiling and crafting) ta eis systasin (the things toward the establishing) of the holy Ekklēsiai. And synekomizon (they brought together) ta ex oikeias spoudēs kai epieikeias (from their own zeal and goodwill) eis ta tēs skēnēs erga all hoi synetoi tē kardia, apoplērountes eikonas (filling out the images) tōn kata kairous didaskalōn (of the teachers in their times), for whom en spoudē kai phrontidi is ergazesthai ta tou Theou, and hosaper an teloiē (whatever may tend) pros onēsin (toward benefit) of the Church of Christ.
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [Completes Exodus 31:2 from §31: φυ|λῆς Ἰούδα.] '…[tri]be of Judah, and ἐνέπλησα (I filled) him with Πνεῦμα θεῖον of σοφία, σύνεσις and ἐπιστήμη. And ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ διανοεῖσθαι (to devise in every work) the χρυσίον, ἀργύριον, χαλκός, the ὑάκινθος (blue/violet), the πορφύρα (purple), the κόκκινον τὸ νηστόν (spun scarlet), the βύσσος ἡ κεκλωσμένη (twisted fine linen), the λιθουργικά (stoneworks), and εἰς τὰ ἔργα τὰ τεκτονικὰ τῶν ξύλων (carpentry of woods) ἐργάζεσθαι κατὰ πάντα τὰ ἔργα. And I δέδωκα (have given/appointed) him, and Ἐλιάβ [son] of Ἀχισαμά, ἐκ φυλῆς Δάν, and to every συνετῷ καρδίᾳ (understanding in heart) δέδωκα σύνεσιν, and they shall ποιήσουσιν all ὅσα συνέταξα (that I ordered).' Ἄθρει (look) how καθηγεῖται (leads) τῶν τεχνουργημάτων (the craftworks) Bezalel, but Eliab ἐργάζεται (works). PALL.: Τί οὖν τοῦτό γε (what then is this)? CYR.: Πεύσῃ (you will learn). Judah and Dan, both ἐξ Ἰακώβ, but the one ἐξ ἐλευθέρας (of the free woman) Leah, the other ἐκ θεραπαίνης (of a maidservant) Bilhah (Βάλη). Τύπος ἐναργής (a clear type), then, is Bezalel of the one πεφηνότος (having appeared) to us ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα τὸ κατὰ σάρκα (as to the flesh), Christ, and ἐκ φύσεως ἀληθῶς τῆς ἐλευθέρας (from the truly free nature), δῆλον ὅτι (clearly) the θεία καὶ ὑπερτάτη (divine and most high). Eliab ἐμφήνειε ἄν (would indicate) εὖ μάλα those who, ὡς ἐκ δούλης τῆς Ἰερουσαλήμ (as from the slave Jerusalem), Χριστῷ συνεργασαμένους (worked with Christ), ἀποστόλους καὶ εὐαγγελιστάς; for they γεγόνασι συνεργοί of God, who μονονουχί (all but) πονοῦντι καὶ τεχνωμένῳ (toiling and crafting) τὰ εἰς σύστασιν (the things toward the establishing) of the holy Ἐκκλησίαι. And συνεκόμιζον (they brought together) τὰ ἐξ οἰκείας σπουδῆς καὶ ἐπιεικείας (from their own zeal and goodwill) εἰς τὰ τῆς σκηνῆς ἔργα all οἱ συνετοὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ, ἀποπληροῦντες εἰκόνας (filling out the images) τῶν κατὰ καιροὺς διδασκάλων (of the teachers in their times), for whom ἐν σπουδῇ καὶ φροντίδι is ἐργάζεσθαι τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, and ὅσαπερ ἂν τελοίη (whatever may tend) πρὸς ὄνησιν (toward benefit) of the Church of Christ.
pass_b_english: Cyril: …of Judah, and I have filled him with the divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding and knowledge, to plan every kind of work in gold, silver and bronze, in blue and purple, in spun scarlet and twisted fine linen, and in stonework, and to work at carpentry in wood in every kind of work. And I myself have appointed both him and Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and to all who have understanding hearts I have given understanding, and they shall make everything that I have commanded’ (Exodus 31:3–6). Notice, then, how Bezalel directs the craftwork, while Eliab carries it out.

Cyril: You will learn. Judah and Dan were both sons of Jacob, but one was born of Leah, a free woman, and the other of Bilhah, a maidservant (Genesis 29:35; 30:5–6). Bezalel, then, is a clear type of Christ, who appeared to us from the tribe of Judah according to the flesh (Hebrews 7:14), and from the nature that is truly free, that is, plainly, the divine and supreme nature. And Eliab would very well represent the apostles and evangelists who worked together with Christ, born as it were of Jerusalem the slave woman (Galatians 4:25). For they became God’s fellow workers (1 Corinthians 3:9), working with him as he, so to speak, labored and crafted all that served to establish the holy churches. And all who had understanding hearts contributed to the works of the tent whatever their own zeal and goodwill supplied, and so served as images of the teachers of every age, for whom it is a matter of zeal and care to do the work of God and whatever may serve the good of the Church of Christ.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-word (φυ|λῆς) completing Exodus 31:2; the quotation runs through Exodus 31:3-6, cited once at its close. Cyril's text of 31:3-4 lacks the LXX's ἀρχιτεκτονῆσαι ἐργάζεσθαι, so διανοεῖσθαι governs the materials directly ('to devise ... the gold'); translated as it stands. ὑάκινθος rendered 'blue' (as in English Bibles). δέδωκα rendered 'appointed' (LXX ἔδωκα αὐτόν; Hebrew 'I have appointed with him'). Eliab son of Ahisamach is the LXX form of the name; English Bibles from the Hebrew call him Oholiab; Cyril's name is kept because his argument rests on him, and the reading page may add '(Oholiab)' if wanted. Leah as mother of Judah: Genesis 29:35; Bilhah as mother of Dan: Genesis 30:5-6 (Cyril spells her Βάλη). 'Free woman' and 'slave' follow Galatians 4:22-26; the explicit phrase 'Jerusalem the slave' matches Galatians 4:25, cited there only. 'From the tribe of Judah according to the flesh' cited to Hebrews 7:14 (ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν); Romans 1:3 and Revelation 5:5 are near but not cited. 'God's fellow workers' = 1 Corinthians 3:9 (θεοῦ γάρ ἐσμεν συνεργοί). μονονουχὶ πονοῦντι καὶ τεχνωμένῳ: the dative refers to God as the master craftsman ('so to speak, labored and crafted'). The contributions of 'all who were wise of heart' take up the phrase of Exodus 31:6 already cited; the bringing of gifts recalls Exodus 35:10, 21-29, but Cyril quotes no verse there, so it is not cited. 'The fruits of their own zeal' renders the neuter τὰ ἐξ οἰκείας σπουδῆς (the things from their own zeal). The source row ends at 'Church of Christ.' with no doxology; the old English added 'to him the glory unto the ages of the ages, Amen', which is not in this Greek and is not translated here; check the PG column end before the book is assembled.

changes: 'a divine Spirit' -> 'the divine Spirit' (an indefinite 'a' with capital Spirit implied one of several divine spirits)
'to devise in every kind of work the gold, the silver ...' (Greek word order) -> 'to plan every kind of work in gold, silver and bronze ...'
emphatic ἐγώ kept: 'And I myself have appointed'
'wise of heart' (dated phrase; συνετός = understanding) -> 'who have/had understanding hearts', both places
'from a nature that is truly free' -> 'from the nature' (τῆς article)
'while he ... labored' read as a contrast; the dative participles go with συνεργοί: now 'working with him as he, so to speak, labored'
'brought in the fruits of their own zeal' ('fruits' added) -> 'contributed ... whatever their own zeal and goodwill supplied'
'give zeal and care to working the things of God' (stiff) -> 'for whom it is a matter of zeal and care to do the work of God'

checked: Exodus 31:3-6 (LXX Eliab = Hebrew Oholiab), Genesis 29:35 (Leah bears Judah), Genesis 30:5-6 (Bilhah bears Dan), Hebrews 7:14, Galatians 4:25, 1 Corinthians 3:9 all match; no doxology in this Greek, none added
